# North Star Metric — Core Revenue

**Core Revenue** — revenue generated by users who are *not* in the
"At Risk" RFM segment (i.e. Champion + Loyal + Promising + New Customer).

## Why this metric, not total revenue

Total revenue treats a $1 purchase from a Champion the same as a $1
purchase from an At-Risk user about to churn — but the two carry very
different future value. Splitting revenue by segment health turns
"are we growing" into "are we growing with customers worth keeping."

## Current baseline (from `user_segments.csv`)

- Total revenue: $6,351,830
- Core Revenue (Champion + Loyal + Promising + New Customer): **$4.73M (74.5%)**
- At-Risk revenue: $1.62M (25.5%) — real revenue today, but from 65,234
  users (59% of all buyers) who are the least likely to purchase again

Tracking Core Revenue alongside total revenue would catch a scenario
total revenue hides: growth driven entirely by one-time, at-risk buyers
while the durable customer base stays flat.

## How to use it

If total revenue grows next quarter, check the Core Revenue split
before declaring success. Growth driven by At-Risk-segment revenue
(one-time buyers, deep discounts, clearance) is a different — and less
durable — story than growth driven by Champion/Loyal spend, even if the
top-line number looks identical.
